content: It is important to take your medication exactly as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately to determine a new dosing schedule. Storage Instructions: Different brands of this medication may have specific storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging for detailed instructions on how to store your specific brand, or ask your pharmacist for guidance. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, headache, or localized pain, bruising, redness, swelling, or itching at the injection site. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. However, it may cause a condition called ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), which can occur during or after treatment. In rare cases, severe OHSS can lead to a sudden buildup of fluid in the abdomen, chest, or heart area. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using cetrorelix, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other products containing gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Stop using this medication if you become pregnant, as it must not be used during pregnancy. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk, but due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Medical Monitoring: While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests, such as vaginal ultrasounds or hormone level assessments, to monitor your progress. Missed Dose: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Formulary Information: Adding plans allows you to compare the formulary status of this drug with others in the same class. To view formulary information, create a list of plans. This list can be saved and edited at any time. Individual plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information.
